I am old now, 72 years, and I farm my small piece here in Mangochi as I have done since I was a boy. These beans I plant together with my maize, the way my father showed me. I have no money for the chemical fertilizer on the beans — even on the maize I struggle, and the beans, they make their own strength in the soil, everyone here knows this. I keep my own seed from last harvest, the same beans I have grown many seasons, and I weed them myself with my hoe when my back allows.
